extracted.intended_audience: General readers of The Spectator / literate public interested in manners, morals, and witty essays (early 18th-century readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Extract normative guidance, behavioural prescriptions, and evaluative observations embedded in Spectator-style short essays on manners, humour, dreams, and virtue. Focus is on rules of conduct, stylistic/normative criteria, and practical maxims the author offers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report only daytime dreams
rubrics_metrics.description: People may dream on as long as they please, but I shall take no Notice of any Imaginary Adventures that do not happen while the Sun is on this Side of the Horizon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author refuses to record or attend to dreams that occur wholly in the night; example: stifling Fritilla's elaborate church-dream because it did not occur in daytime. Implicit rule for reporting dreams: only those that intersect waking-daylight matter for public consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use noisy morning criers as reminders (do not suppress them)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead therefore of suppressing this Order of Mortals, I would propose it to my Readers to make the best Advantage of their Morning Salutations...a Citizen who is waked by one of these Criers, may regard him as a kind of Remembrancer, come to admonish him that it is time to return to the Circumstances he has overlooked all the Night-time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than seeing city criers, watchmen, or other early noisy people as nuisances, treat them as salutary interruptions that return you from fanciful imaginations to real obligations. Examples: Several people owe deliverances from misfortunes to being awakened (small-coalman, watchman, carman, cinder-wench). Advice rejects suppression and recommends appropriation of their function as salutary reminders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance merriness and seriousness (avoid extremes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most perfect Character is that which is formed out of both of them. A Man would neither chuse to be a Hermit nor a Buffoon: Humane Nature is not so miserable, as that we should be always melancholy; nor so happy, as that we should be always merry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both merry and serious dispositions have virtues and vices; the ideal character mixes chearfulness and thoughtful seriousness. Practical implication for conduct and for portraying characters: avoid one-note affect; cultivate a temper that can be serious when needed and merry at proper seasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merriness must be seasonable and not dominate discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: The merry Part of the World are very amiable, whilst they diffuse a Chearfulness through Conversation at proper Seasons and on proper Occasions; but, on the contrary, a great Grievance to Society, when they infect every Discourse with insipid Mirth, and turn into Ridicule such Subjects as are not suited to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laughter and wit are positive (the philosophers regard laughter as property of reason), but excess or misapplied mirth is folly and social nuisance. Criterion for good humour: appropriateness of topic and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seriousness should be accompanied by cheerfulness and humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: On the other Side, Seriousness has its Beauty whilst it is attended with Chearfulness and Humanity, and does not come in unseasonably to pall the good Humour of those with whom we converse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gravitas is praiseworthy only when humane and not sourly censorious; seriousness that wrecks others' good humour or is unseasonable is blameworthy. Example: the statesman who, retiring from public life, advised visitors 'Be serious' as a guard against temptation — seriousness as a stabilising virtue, not as social dampener.

rubrics_metrics.name: Levity weakens moral resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: It must indeed be confessed that Levity of Tamper takes a Man off his Guard, and opens a Pass to his Soul for any Temptation that assaults it. It favours all the Approaches of Vice, and weakens all the Resistance of Virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cautionary principle: habitual frivolity predisposes to moral failure. Practical prescription: cultivate seriousness where moral vigilance is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Afternoon nap as a productive indulgence
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been my Custom, as I grow old, to allow my self in some little Indulgencies... Among others is that of an Afternoon's Napp... By this means I enjoy a double Morning, and rise twice-a-day fresh to my Speculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Napping is recommended as a legitimate restorative that increases productive waking hours and provokes instructive dreams; anecdotal support (author's productive dreams). Minor caveat implied later: beware of overindulgence that would spoil one's 'spectators' or natural talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform excessive levity by measured constraint (Trophonius's Cave metaphor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cave... disposed the Person who was in it to be more pensive and thoughtful than ordinary...no Man was ever observed to laugh all his Life after, who had once made his Entry into this Cave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphorical prescription: tools or interventions (social, educational, or institutional) can convert the excessively merry into appropriately serious persons. Examples from the dream: comic actors, fops, coquets transformed to grave figures — but note risk: a comedian who tried to lose laugh lines became too solid and lost suitability for comic roles (warning against overcorrection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forming benevolent habits requires persistent practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A great deal may be done by a Course of Beneficence obstinately persisted in; this...being a likely way of establishing a moral Habit...these last [moral habits] must be continually reinforced with fresh Supplies, or they will languish and die away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral and charitable dispositions are maintained only by repeated action; unlike bodily habits, they do not change physical constitution and therefore need ongoing reinforcement. Practical implication: schedule and persist in acts of beneficence to form durable virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three chief checks on benevolence: bodily temperament, love of the world, uneasiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The first and leading Cause is an unhappy Complexion of Body... Another Thing which suspends the Operations of Benevolence, is the Love of the World... The last Enemy to Benevolence I shall mention is Uneasiness of any Kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnosis: identify which of the three is operating (inherited irritable constitution; acquisitive jealousy from scarce worldly goods; personal discontent or guilt). Remedies implied: patient habit-formation for constitutional defects; moderation in desire for worldly goods; address internal unease (restore calm, contentment) to reopen capacity for charity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer virtue and shared goods to solitary wealth; virtue grows by communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue is a Good of a nobler kind; it grows by Communication, and so little resembles earthly Riches, that the more Hands it is lodged in, the greater is every Man's particular Stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative economic-moral principle: unlike finite material goods, moral goods (virtue, benevolence) increase when shared. Practical consequence: cultivate and spread virtue rather than hoarding wealth; desire only necessary worldly goods to avoid envy and competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time requests well: ask favors when the other is in good humour
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a Favour to request of any one, to observe the softest times of Address, when the Soul, in a Flush of good Humour, takes a Pleasure to shew it self pleased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactical interpersonal rule: choose moments of receptivity (good humour, contentment) when soliciting assistance or making requests to increase success; avoid asking during uneasiness, discontent, or distraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not live as if there were no God or no men (moral balance injunction)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Man should not live as if there was no God in the World; nor, at the same Time, as if there were no Men in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise ethical maxim: balance spiritual seriousness with social engagement; recognize duties both to the divine and to fellow humans. Applied as guidance for character and conduct—neither ascetic otherworldliness nor thoughtless worldly abandon is correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induce dreams (anecdotal method) — eat bride-cake under pillow
rubrics_metrics.description: The Writer...had fasted all that Day; and that he might be sure of dreaming upon something at Night, procured an handsome Slice of Bride-Cake, which he placed very conveniently under his Pillow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anecdotal, quasi-folk method for provoking dreams: place bride-cake under the pillow. Caveat in text: the writer's memory failed and the cake was eaten, suggesting the unpredictable effectiveness and the foolishness of attributing too much to such contrivances.
